subject: POC trial planning: model selection and success criteria
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: POC trial planning: model selection and success criteria

Hi Lisa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a proposed plan for the POC so we can get the trial kicked off next week: 

Summary of background
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood inference for product help chat across English + Spanish/Portuguese. Primary focus on accuracy and latency under production-like load.
- Key constraint: Data residency requirement for EU customers (we'll keep that in mind for future expansion).

Proposed success criteria (please confirm/edit):
1) Quality: >= 85% helpfulness on a 100-example eval set (manual scoring by your SMEs) and <2% hallucination rate on factual prompts.
2) Latency: p95 end-to-end generation time <= 500ms on standard user prompts (baseline seq length ~150 tokens).
3) Cost: Target token cost < $X per 1k tokens (we'll refine after initial runs).
4) Stability: No more than 2 incidents affecting SLA during the 3-week trial.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Day 0 (Kickoff): share evaluation prompt set, access, and POC plan (attached).
- Week 1: Baseline runs across candidate models, measure latency/cost/quality.
- Week 2–3: Focused tuning (prompt templates, batching, KV caching), run multilingual test pass.
- End of Week 3: Final evaluation and readout (we'll produce a short report with token-level cost breakdown and recommended model/profile).

Ownership
- Globex POC lead: Lisa Chen (you) — provide evaluation prompts, SME scoring.
- Redwood SE: Marissa Cole — experiment setup, instrumentation, quality monitoring.
- Redwood infra/eng contact: Aditya Rao — integration and any private deployment questions.

Model selection recommendations (open models) — primary and fallback
- Primary (recommended start): Mistral-8x7B (instruction-tuned) quantized (4-bit). Good balance of cost/latency and strong instruction-following for chat.
- Fallback: Llama-2-13B (q4) — fallback for cases where Mistral shows weakness on some multilingual prompts; higher quality on some factual tasks at modest latency increase.
- Optional heavier candidate (if you need stronger reasoning): Falcon-40B (non-quantized / q4) — higher cost and latency, use only for a small subset of hard prompts.

Multilingual notes
- We will profile English + Spanish + Portuguese prompt sets. If we see degraded Spanish/Portuguese quality on Mistral, we will test Llama-2-13B and Falcon-40B variants as fallbacks.
- For region-specific residency (if later required) we can run models in eu-west-1 and route traffic accordingly.

Next steps (action items)
- Ben: I will upload the POC plan and set up a shared Drive folder (attached).
- Lisa: please confirm success criteria and share the 100-eval prompts or a sample subset by Friday.
- Marissa/Aditya: please confirm availability for kickoff call (propose Mon 2026-06-15).

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf (POC scope and instrumentation checklist)

Thanks — looking forward to running this with you.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this looks good and aligns with our internal expectations. A few clarifications and confirmations from our side: 

1) Success criteria: Agreed to the quality and latency targets; on cost we'll let you propose a concrete target after baseline runs.
2) Multilingual: English + Spanish are must-haves; Portuguese is also important for one of our markets, so please include it in the multilingual pass.
3) Fallbacks: We agree with the primary use of Mistral-8x7B. For Portuguese, if quality dips we want Llama-2-13B as a fallback. For a small set of enterprise KB retrieval prompts we may ask to test Falcon-40B.
4) Timeline: Kickoff on Mon 2026-06-15 works for us; Lisa (me) and our ML engineer Diego will join.

Attached is the signed NDA (globex-nda-signed.pdf) — Procurement looped in. I uploaded the initial 40 evaluation prompts; we'll expand to 100 after kickoff.

Thanks — Lisa
